html:
SMTO-CMP-0043 — SMTO can't finish the task while background work is still running

GUID: 7c15af8a-a597-4484-b623-bb09160f223b
Slug: completion-background-activities-pending
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The task tried to finish, but work it started in the background hasn't ended yet. The answer so far and any finished results are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through the steps listed under this task for any that still show as running, waiting for approval, or waiting for your reply. SMTO only finishes the task after every required background step has ended.
  2. If a step shows Review approval or Provide input, open it and respond, or reply in the conversation if SMTO is waiting for your answer. A background step that is waiting on you can't end by itself, so the task stays open.
  3. If a step has run far longer than expected and you no longer need it, select the Stop button beside that step. Stopping does not undo what it already did. Stopping ends that unfinished background work, so the task no longer waits for it.
  4. Before asking SMTO to run that work again, open the step and read its output to see whether it already ran. The background work may already have made its changes, and repeating it could make them twice.

What success looks like

  • No steps under the task show as running or waiting, and the task shows Completed with its answer.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking again. Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same request just to make the task finish; the background work may already have run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion validation blocked the task's finish because the background policy requires waiting for required activities and at least one completion-required background activity is still active or waiting.

What this means

  • Background policy requires waiting for required activities and at least one such activity is still in an active or waiting state. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Background policy requires waiting for required activities and at least one such activity is still in an active or waiting state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect required flags, effective wait policy and exact activity states.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the activity_ids listed in the requirements against the run's background_activities (state, completion_required) and the effective background policy ('Wait for required activities before finish' in Agent Checks). Let active activities reach a terminal state, answer waiting_user/waiting_approval prompts or cancel unneeded activities; do not launch duplicate work to make the completion check pass.
  • Inspect the required background activities and wait for their authoritative terminal results before completing the task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect existing activities and their effects. Do not launch duplicate work to make the completion check pass.

How to verify the fix

  • Required background work settles with authoritative results under the accepted policy.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
